title: Keys To Exalting A Nation Part 2
paragraphs: Our theme this year is good governance. Our focus is on understanding the principles of successful nations. What makes a country successful? In fact, what constitutes a successful state? We will discuss this topic in this session. I know I will not finish it, so please follow along with me in the next few sessions as we focus on this important topic. This semester is not just about personal success, but also about national impact. Therefore, this session addresses the concept of national influence.

I would like to begin with a statement concerning the divine origins of nations. Where did nations begin? I want to start from here to explain the current situation to you. God's intention from the beginning was to establish a heavenly nation on Earth. That was God's original idea. His plan, and his goal in creating the earth, is for people to inhabit it. Secondly, God’s divine goal was to establish a heavenly colony on Earth. Therefore, it was God's vision that there should be a heavenly nation on Earth.

God wanted to establish a heavenly colony on Earth. His divine goal was to establish a heavenly culture on Earth. Write all of this down because it is the greatest message you can share with others: that God’s plan, his idea, and his original intention was to establish a state, a heavenly nation on earth, to embody a heavenly culture on earth. His strategy for achieving this was through establishing a heavenly government on Earth. Government, therefore, is the key to establishing a nation.

Therefore, the primary purpose of government is to make and administer the law that governs life in the nation. It also produces the culture of the nation. Perhaps this last statement is the most important one that I will present to you throughout this night. What is the primary purpose of government? Here is the answer: The purpose of government is to make and administer the law, and this law regulates people's lives, and this life shapes the culture of the country.

Therefore, I want you to understand the relationship between government, law, people, and culture. The government makes the law, the law regulates people's lifestyle, and lifestyle becomes the culture. Therefore, the most important element in any country is the government, because it controls what happens in the country and what it becomes. The government also controls people and what people become, because the law regulates their way of life. Is this clear?

Therefore, whoever makes the law is a dangerous group, because they organize and create through it. This leads me to another point: the fact that we were created to rule the earth. God did this because He knew that in order for the earth to become like heaven, He had to put us on earth and make everything under our control. Then he gave us his law to be the law of the land. Let us read from the Constitution of Heaven, Section Eight, Paragraph Four, for those who are interested.

Psalm 8, verse 4: David was a king, not a religious man, but a politician. David asked: What is man that your mind should be filled with him? Oh God, why do you think so much about human beings? What is the importance of the Son of Man that makes you care about what happens to him and what he does? Then David himself answered, saying: I know why we are so important. You have made us a little lower than you. This word begins with the word "Elohim," which means God. Then what did you crown us with?

Say it loudly: With glory and honor. You have been taught not to touch the glory of God, and this is a religious saying, not a kingdom saying. The Kingdom says that you have been given the glory of God. What is the meaning of glory? It is a word derived from the word "caporte," which is actually related to nature or culture. You have been crowned with the culture of God, with the nature of God. That makes sense.

If God wanted the nature of heaven to be present on earth, then He had to place it in the creatures He created on it. Because culture is not in the land, but in the people. There is no culture in any part of your country. People are the ones who carry the culture. Culture is the glory of a people, and it is their true nature. Therefore, it is the nature of the people that is brought about in the land. The Bible says that He crowned you with what? With glory. And most importantly, the honor.

This means that God has elevated you to the ranks of the great. Honoring means elevating, appreciating, and respecting. The Bible says that He crowned you with glory, with the culture of God and honor. God respects his creatures, he respects his children, and he is proud of us. He says: " Go forth and possess the land." Look at the following statement: “ And you made him master over the works of your hands, and you put everything under man’s feet.” Do you need any more convincing about why you are here?

You did not come from the earth, but you came to it. You are from heaven. You have been sent here to rule the earth on behalf of God, to spread the glory of God, the nature of God, and the culture of God on earth. Therefore, you are the first government, and the only government that God has put on Earth. And governance means, of course, applying justice on a certain land. Justice is linked to the law. This means applying your country's laws to the environment in which you live.

God has placed you here, and how many things are under your feet? everything. This means every animal, every dog, every cat, every plant, every gold, silver, oil, oceans, mountains, and trees. You rule the physical planet, and subject it to the influence of the culture of Heaven. That's why you were sent here. So you are the first government, and what is the purpose of government? Write this down: The essence of government is the law. Remember this well. The essence of government is the law.

Governments do many things, and you may think you understand their importance, but the most important thing a government does is debate, legislation, and passing laws. We now have some legislation before parliamentarians that deals with important issues, and some of you may not realize the extent of the impact of what is happening. Therefore, you must give your opinion, because they are about to pass a law. When you think about government, you should think about the law.

This is why those aspiring to power in any country seek to gain access to Congress or the House of Representatives, as these are the bodies that legislate the laws that become effective. Everyone wants to control the legislative process. This leads us to the second point: whoever controls or enacts the law creates the nation. Never ignore those who fight for the laws. Some of you may wonder why there are so many people in our countries who are fighting for laws that protect same-sex marriage, for example.

This is no easy task. They do not care about your religious gatherings. They don't care about your discussions in church. All that matters to them is that the law becomes effective, because once it does, the nation becomes a nation based on this type of relationship. Government is based on law, and law is the foundation of the nation. This leads me to the third point: the law is what creates and controls culture. What did you say? The law is what creates and controls culture.

Therefore, a nation becomes what it is based on the laws made by those in power, and this power is called the government. They govern the nation with laws, and it is the law that produces culture. This leads me to the fourth point: The first thing God gave to Moses when he wanted to create a nation of slaves was the law. God gave him the law before He gave him the land, because He knew that if the land was given without a law, it would be a land without a law. Land cannot be regulated except through law.

Therefore, God gave Moses the law first, and then the people were given the land later. This leads me to point five: Whoever controls the drafting of the law controls the quality of the nation. Who controls what? On the drafting of the law. Who controls the quality of the nation? Again, she wonders why people want to stay in positions of power.

Because when you are in a position of power that allows you to make and influence the laws of a country, you are in fact controlling the quality of that country, its values, and its moral standards. This leads us to point six, which I consider extremely dangerous. The rule of law depends on those who govern it. This is a quote by Miles Munro. You can post it now on Twitter. I will repeat it: the rule of law depends on those who govern it.

Democracy, for example, prides itself on being a philosophy of the rule of law. What they mean by that is that the law governs the state. But we forget that the law that governs the state is made by the men who govern it. Therefore, simply saying that the law governs the state does not necessarily mean that you have a good state; it may be that the wrong law governs it. This is how dangerous governments are. Governments are able to control and change laws.

They have the power to legislate and incite even to change the constitution, because once you rule the law, the law rules you. So, yes, we support the rule of law, but the question is: who rules the law? They can change the law. Have you ever wondered why the Bible calls God's laws " laws"? Do you know why they are called laws? The word " statue" is the same as the word " figure". It's like that statue in the middle of your city. There is a lady in the middle of our country. She's been there all my life.

Many of you were born while she was there. You will die, and she will remain there. It has been there for almost 180 years. She never moved. What is it called? A statue. God used this term for His word, for His law. He says: "My law is laws." This means you do n't change it by voting. Do not modify it with any work of human creation. That woman sitting in our courtyard, what is her name? Queen Victoria. Queen Victoria. She has survived all the hurricanes that have hit the Bahamas. Isn't that so? It didn't budge.

In other words, the currents were flowing around her, but she withstood them all. And when the currents receded, they remained the same. As you can see, there is a lot to be said. Have you ever heard this talk? What is the prevailing trend in your society? Many things are currents, meaning they come to affect you, and governments must realize which laws should not be changed. The only laws you can be sure will not be changed are those given to you by the Creator.

There are some things that the Creator has set up, and we tamper with them. I learned something years ago. If you went downtown to that woman, Queen Victoria, and said to her, "I hate you," and made a fist and punched her in the face with all your might because you wanted to change her, what would happen to your fist? It will turn into a mass of blood. Do you know why? Whatever you do, she will not follow you, you will follow her. You don't break it, it breaks you. That's how all principles and laws are.

You do not break God's laws, but you break yourself with them. No matter how hard we try to change the fixed laws of nature and the laws of physiological facts, we will be the ones broken, not the laws. That's why I don't panic when I see people trying to shout at God, "This is what we're going to do." Whatever you say, I smile because I know you can't change a divine law. Divine laws are always manifested in natural law, and natural law does not respect human law. This is very important.

Therefore, the rule of law depends on those who govern it. For this reason, even laws made by humans cannot be trusted. This leads me to what happened when Adam fell. First, the first thing God gave to Adam was judgment. The word " sovereignty," as we know, means the authority of the kingdom. God said to Adam: "Have dominion over the earth." We read that in Psalm 8, verse 4, where God said: “ You have been given authority over the earth.” So, God was giving Adam first and foremost the power to rule. Why?

Because governance is the most important element in leading and influencing the land. This leads us to the second point: when Adam disobeyed God, he committed a great betrayal. This means that God trusted Adam and gave him authority. When you breach trust in authority, it is called high treason, and its punishment is death. Therefore, the fall of man was not only a loss for the family, but also a loss of his relationship with the government of Heaven, and a loss of the government of Heaven's commitment to Earth.

Thus, the fall of humanity was like the departure of the ruler of Heaven, who is the Spirit of God. The Holy Spirit was sent to us to be the ruler of the earth. When we disobeyed the laws of Heaven, the ruler departed, and thus the fall of man was the loss of the Kingdom of Heaven and its rule over the earth. We have lost a government. Therefore, we have lost the nation of Heaven. And remember now that we are trying to figure out how to restore the nations to their rightful place?

How do we make a heavenly or heaven-like nation? Well, how did the nation become heavenly? Is this the correct word? Heavenly. The original nation that was here with Adam was heavenly because the ruler of heaven, the Holy Spirit, dwelt within it. Adam was guided by the Holy Spirit, not by his flesh. When Adam followed his flesh, he lost that heavenly influence, and the Bible says that the Holy Spirit was no longer able to struggle with humans. And so the Holy Spirit departed. Is this clear?

When the Holy Spirit departed from the earth, the government departed from it. Just like in the Bahamas, Jamaica, Barbados, St. Kitts and Thomas, St. Lucia, or anywhere else. Wherever a colony exists, the moment it disobeys your ruling kingdom, the ruler is summoned. This happened here in the Bahamas in 1973. When that ruler is removed from power, the reign of that government ends. The last British governor here was in 1973. When that ruler left, we lost the control of Great Britain over us.

Therefore, nothing in the Bahamas is under the control of England. When a ruler is removed, the government is removed. When the Holy Spirit descended upon the earth because of our rebellion against God, the kingdom of heaven descended upon the earth. Is this clear? So, God's goal was to restore that government. Now, we know what God has done, don't we? God called a man named Abraham. Of course, Noah, as you know, is the one who called him to save humanity. But then God called a man named Abraham.

What did God say to Abraham? Let's look at Genesis 18:18. It is very important to read what God said to him. God says: "O Abraham, you will become a great and powerful nation." This is important. It is not a religion called Judaism. God's plan was never a religion. Abraham is not the founder of a religion, but the father of a nation. God says, "O Abraham, I will make you a great and powerful nation." It seems that there are two essential things for the success of any nation: greatness and power.

Now, we must discover how to become great and how to become strong. God guided Abraham on how to achieve this, and then said: "And all the nations of the earth will be blessed through you." Can I say it another way? All the nations of the earth will be influenced by you. Can I say it another way? All other nations will take you as a model. Why? Because God wanted only one nation on Earth. Why? Because He created only one race on Earth, and that is the human race.

There is no white race, no black race, no red race, no brown race, and no yellow race. In the Bible, there is only one race, and that is the human race. God wants this race to be the ruler of the earth, but we have lost that government. Thus God says to Abraham: Since I have lost all races, that is, the nations of the earth, I will make you an example for all nations. We know what happened. Of course, Moses took on this responsibility later and went to God and his people.

Now, look at Exodus 19:5, completing this process. God says: If you obey me completely and keep my covenant, then you will be what among all nations. A chosen people, and the whole earth is mine, though I own everything. You will be mine as a nation, a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. Again, God never asked Moses to establish a religion. What was he seeking? A nation. Now, what is our topic for this session? Glorifying a nation. God cares about the Bahamas, not the churches. Oh, my God. Be quiet now.

Look at that. Look, the problem is that we were so focused on going to heaven that we forgot our mission on Earth. In fact, religion abandons the earth in its theology. The first command from God to man was to rule over what? On Earth, not to go to Heaven. We came from heaven. God says: “ This matter concerns your influence on the earth, and becoming the ruling nation over it.” Therefore God said to Moses: Tell them, I will make them a royal priesthood.

This means a vertical relationship with God, and the holy nation. This is the horizontal impact of the people. The priest is the one who stands between God and the earth. Do you understand? The nation means influence on the ground. Therefore, the holy priesthood means that the people who rule the earth must have a vertical relationship with God. Are you with me? Therefore, monarchy and priesthood are intertwined. Monarchy and priesthood. Priesthood means vertical. Ownership means horizontally.

Are you still with me? You should write that down. What does "priest" mean? Vertical relationship. What does ownership mean? Horizontally. Therefore, in order to fulfill God’s will as ruler of the earth, I must first have a relationship with God. This is the priestly relationship. Then I can exercise royal influence on the land. This is the horizontal side. Therefore, every leader in our country must, first and foremost, have a vertical relationship with God.

Then it must be trusted to have a vertical and horizontal impact on our country and our lives. Therefore, we should not trust the people who have the power to rule on Earth. Rather, we must first trust those who have a connection to the authority in heaven. Okay. What will you be? First, a kingdom of priests. A kingdom is a state, a ruling state, a state government. The holy nation is the one that is influenced by these priests. Therefore, in God's eyes, there is no difference between a priest and a king.

The king is a priest and the priest is a king. They are the same in the eyes of God. We have a theology that separates them. In the Old Testament, if you read the Bible carefully, you will find this interesting. The person who ordained the king was always the prophet. The prophet appointed the king, which means that the person who had a vertical relationship gave permission to the person who had a horizontal relationship. Samuel laid his hands on David and Saul. And that's how it's supposed to be.

But the situation is different in our modern countries. We resort to the Attorney General or another authority to obtain our authority. In other words, the principle is that judgment begins with the relationship. Write this down. What does the ruling begin with? In relation. If you have a relationship, you are qualified to judge. If you are a priest first, you can become a president. If you are a priest, you can become prime minister. This does not necessarily mean that you are religious.

Rather, it means that you have a relationship with God to be in touch with the laws of Heaven, so that you do not violate them with the laws of Earth. And again, this is how a nation that glorifies the Lord is built. God says: It is better that you inform the country about this program. Now, I want you to look. What is a nation? What is a nation? We are talking about the nation. Write this down.

A nation is a group of people bound by a common heritage, a common language, a common land, common Jewish wisdom, common ideals, and common values, and these people are subject to the rule of one God. In our country, we believe that the path we take will only end with the multiplicity of gods, or perhaps with a number of them. But in our country we decided: One God.

This means that it is very difficult to have an atheist in parliament, because according to the aspirations of our constitution and our national anthem, which embodies our desire to sing it, a person who does not believe in one God cannot lead us. Therefore, no one who is an atheist in his theological view of life should rule our country. If our country wants to have a single point of reference, this is an important definition. Let me tell you why God did what He did.

When God brought the Israelites out of Egypt, He said to Moses: “ I want to create a nation from them.” The first thing God gave them was a list of laws. The Ten Commandments were the foundation for the creation of God’s ideal nation. It was a list of laws. But what is important in the laws, perhaps you have forgotten. The first law, which is part of the Ten Commandments, is: You shall have no other gods before me. God began with God. It did not begin with "Do not steal, do not kill, do not lie," etc.

He said, "First and foremost, let's determine who holds supreme authority." Because if a nation does not declare who its god is, then the laws will be subject to the whims of men. Okay. Without a higher authority, everything is relative. Without fear, there is no wisdom. Oh, have you lost focus? Good. If there is no god to fear, you will do anything. For this reason, fearing God is the beginning of wise choices. That's what it means.

If you fear breaking the law of your authority, it will discipline you in enacting laws. This is why those who want to change God’s laws always seek to get rid of God first. They remove him from parliament, the Senate, the law, the courts, and the schools. Because if they could get rid of God, they would not fear angering any authority, and therefore they would be able to enact any law they wanted. Therefore, the first thing that God revealed to Moses was the Law. But what was the first law revealed to him about?

By the god they will worship. For this reason, it is very important for nations to have a clear reference to God. May I ask you this? The preamble to our constitution in the Bahamas contains a very important clause, and we continually demand that it be enshrined in the constitution as law. But they reject that because, you know, they say in democracy—which I consider a problem in itself—that you can dictate to people what they should believe.

But I think what needs to be done is for you to declare your beliefs, and then they can come and live with you as long as they do not contradict your beliefs. It seems you are all silent, but I can try it myself. Anyway, come to my house, and live according to my rules. You can live in my house, but according to my rules. Don't come to my house and impose your own rules. I don't use profanity, and neither do you. This is correct.

As you know, people can come and live in the Bahamas, but they shouldn't come and dictate to the Bahamas what they should believe. If the Bahamas have already declared their God, then blessed is the nation whose God is known as the Lord. Good? Therefore, if you do not identify the Lord, your nation will not be blessed or exalted. Let me tell you about the components of the nation. Please write this down. Hey guys, write this down. What makes a nation a nation? This is extremely important. First, one land. One land.

Secondly, a unified national vision. Third, one language. Fourth, one constitution. Fifth, a set of unified laws. Sixth, one government. Let me talk about this a little. We have an island in the Bahamas. Viewers may not know this, but we have 700 islands in the Bahamas. One of our islands in the Bahamas has a separate government, not ours. This island is in a difficult situation, because there cannot be two governments in one country.

This island is called Grand Bahama, and the government located there runs a city called Freeport. The problem is that two governments cannot exist together, because if the two rulers are the same people, there cannot be two different sets of laws, taxes, etc. They say: "Any creature with two heads is a monster." This is why there is confusion on that island in the Bahamas. Confusion is evident in the people.

People are under psychological pressure, and therefore it is difficult for any government to dictate to another if the latter is given the powers to govern. When you have two governments in a country, you lose the status of a state. You have a split and frustration. That is why God created man with one head in his body. You have billions of cells with one head and one brain. You don't have two brains, you don't have two minds. Therefore, it is very important to understand that there must be one government. Good.

Point seven: The existence of one common principle that constitutes the state. The principle, for example, America's principle is freedom. This is the principle. Everything is freedom. The principle is freedom. Of course, the concept of freedom must be regulated because freedom without law is tyranny. So when you say you want freedom, what else should you want? the law. Okay, that's point five. There can be no freedom without laws. The number nine out of eight: the countries share the same values.

The number nine out of eight: common morals. Number ten: Shared culture. Number eleven: Common standards. Number twelve: The shared national commitment to defend the homeland. Number thirteen: A nation must have a common standard, which is its flag. In fact, the Hebrew word for "science" means "standard". For this reason, when they fought battles throughout history, they always raised the flag at the front. The flag bearer was not carrying any weapon, but was surrounded by a team that protected him at all times.

The battle was never lost until the flag of the other army fell. The goal of winning the war is to eliminate science. The moment the soldier carrying the flag falls, another soldier catches him. Why? Because they cannot let science fall. Have you heard of this before? Do not let old science fall because science is the standard. Now, the word "standard" refers to the embodiment of the state. Therefore, science is not just a piece of cloth.

For this reason, if you wear the flag in a certain way on your body, you could be imprisoned. This is called desecration of science. If you burn the animal flag, you may be imprisoned because you are burning the people. You are burning a symbol of the state. That's why, when you say "Science Day," it's not a joke. You cannot have two flags in one country. This is very important. Two flags represent two peoples. Good? I want you to understand the meaning of countries.

I'm sure many of you have seen that picture; I think it's from World War II, when the soldiers appear. There is now a statue of soldiers raising the flag. Have you seen the statue? It is not just an ordinary statue. Did you know that flags are so important that the national anthem of the United States is neither about God nor about the people? It's about a piece of cloth. Well, you didn't know that. e. If you sing the American national anthem, it's about a piece of cloth.

The entire anthem revolves around a piece of cloth. Look at how she thinks. Good. Can someone sing it for me? It's about science. It's all about science, and do you know what they sing about? They sing about what they call ancient glory. What is glory? It is the essence of the people. Now, do you remember during the American Civil War in 1776 when they fought the British? The British, remember, ruled America just as they ruled us, and the Americans who fled Europe fought against the British.

They sent them back to their homes. The goal was to keep that flag flying. When the British returned, the flag was still standing. They said it was torn, but it was still standing. It had holes, but it was still standing. Therefore, the American national anthem is about the flag, because you should only have one flag in every nation. Are you learning something new tonight? Let's sing the American national anthem. Can anyone sing it? How do you begin, Reverend Richard? Oh, can you see in the early morning light?

Notice that they are now talking about the light of early dawn. This means that when the sun rose that morning, the flag was still flying. What is the next verse? The light of early dawn. How proudly we cheered as the twilight shimmered with its red streaks and bright stars. Look, no one is afraid to go through the perilous night. Do you see that? Oh, they're still standing. He waved all night, and our flag was still there. Oh, say that starry flag. banner. Okay. And the home of the brave. It's all about a piece of cloth. Amen. Now, if you read the Bible, if you have an electronic copy of it, type the word "banner" in the search box and press search, and you will find it throughout the Bible, and it all talks about science. Therefore, each country should have one flag. Never allow different flags to enter your country as a symbol. Note the third point, which is the single language.

Do you know that language is very important? Because encouraging linguistic diversity destroys the country. How did God destroy the Tower of Babel project? He did not attack them, but confused their languages ​​so that they could not understand each other. They couldn't even tell the man who brought the piece of wood. Therefore, they were unable to build the country because of the differences in languages. No country should encourage multilingualism.

Now, if you read the story of the Tower of Babel, or "The Chatterbox," it was named so because that word was used to describe what happened to them. They were gossiping. Have you ever said "Stop the chatter"? This means stopping the chatter. It means the Tower of Babel, the tower of confused language. This is the story in Genesis 11. Read it tonight. It is a story about the destruction of a country due to multilingualism. They started gossiping.

For this reason, it is very important for you, as a people wherever you are, as a nation watching this program, to pay attention to the requirements for learning different languages ​​to live in a country. As you know, I have no problem with you learning a language for commerce or a language for work, but that shouldn't be the norm in the country. Anyone who comes to your country must learn your language. Let me share another piece of information with you.

The first time the Holy Spirit descended to Earth in the Bible among humans was to destroy language. This is mentioned in Genesis, chapter 11. The first time the Holy Spirit returned to Earth was in Jerusalem in a small room. Good. And the first thing he brought back was one language. They all spoke in tongues. In other words, God scattered the languages ​​in Genesis 11, then put them back together again and again in Acts 2.

Therefore, when I travel around the world and meet people whose native language I do not understand, as soon as we enter a place of worship, they begin to speak in tongues. I feel at home because tongues are a common language for all believers. So I visit all these countries with multiple languages, but in a worshipful experience with God, they begin to speak in tongues, and we all look the same. God has restored one language.

Nothing is more dangerous than people speaking the same language, because they may now believe the same thing, and they may say the same things. This is what is called unity. Is this okay? Good. Each country should have one common reference point, and this is a very important reference point. It concerns your God. A state cannot exist without a single reference point. God says to the Israelites: You shall have no other gods before me. Then he says: Do not make idols carved from anything I have created.

Secondly, do not worship any other god. God was clear. He now says: " Now we can talk about honoring parents, not stealing, and so on. Take a break daily, or weekly, and take care of yourself, and don't be careless. But first let's clarify things. There is no god but God." The reason this is important, and I hope you understand me, is that democracy without God is a humanistic tendency. Yes. What is humanism? Some of you may have studied it in school or university.

Humanism is the idea that man is the standard of right and wrong, good and evil, truth and falsehood. Human beings become the standard. This is humanism. In other words, man is God. Now, if you study the concept of democracy, you will find that it is based on the premise that man is the authority. They say that power is in the hands of the people. Do you remember that? They say that the majority of the people decide what is good or right. Now we have to decide whether we want to follow this approach.

This means that no matter how wrong something seems, if most people agree with it, they can justify it. naturally. So, the problem is that if there is a divine reference, then if you and I come up with an idea, a bill, legislation, or law for discussion, we must refer to its standard. If he is not the reference, then we are the ones who decide whether he is right or wrong. This is what is called humanity. Humanity is embodied in a word you must write down again: relativity.

Relativism simply means that things are good or bad based on what is relative to you. It's relative. If you think it's good, then leave me alone. I'll do what I like, and mind your own business. If I liked it, then I liked it. If you don't like it, leave me alone. This is relativity. Relativity also states that there is no absolute truth. Truth is relative, as they say, and depends on a person's point of view. Yes, it is what is called situational ethics.

What is ethical depends on the prevailing circumstances, which means that there is no fixed standard by which anything can be measured. Many people strongly desire this because they want to impose their opinion. A nation that has no reference point by which to measure its rightness or wrongness is a human nation. Let me mention the term used in my country for this meaning, which is secularism. Secularism is simply humanity wrapped in an elegant veneer.

When they say, and I have heard them say in our parliament, "We are a secular state," they mean that we do not believe that truth is the monopoly of anyone, and we do not want anyone to dictate to us what is right or wrong.
